title: 在线数据选择与动态配比

claims.claim: Curriculum Learning studies organizing training examples progressively rather than uniformly sampling all examples from the beginning.
claims.notes: Curriculum schedules vary; no universal 20/50/30 training-step schedule is asserted.

claims.claim: DoReMi learns domain mixture proportions using a small reference model and proxy model with Group DRO on excess loss, before transferring proportions to a target LM.
claims.notes: Proxy-stage adaptive weighting does not mean the target LM continually reoptimizes its mixture.

claims.claim: DoReMi excess loss is measured relative to the reference model, so naively prioritizing raw high loss would not reproduce the DoReMi method.
claims.locator: Under the hood: excess loss and Group DRO optimizer
claims.notes: The Stanford authors' explanation supports the distinction; underlying equation belongs to the cited DoReMi paper.

claims.claim: RegMix trains multiple small models with different mixtures, fits a regression to predict performance of unseen mixtures, and selects a mixture for larger-model pretraining.
claims.notes: The proxy-to-target transfer is empirical under the paper's model/data/evaluation conditions.

claims.claim: RegMix-D models proxy training trajectories to predict stage-specific mixtures and supports both offline schedule planning and online loss-adaptive variants.
claims.locator: Abstract; offline and online deployment variants
claims.notes: Publication is Findings of IJCNLP-AACL 2026, not a claim about all dynamic data-mixing algorithms.

claims.claim: Efficient Online Data Mixing combines bandit-style online selection with domain data mixture updates during LM pretraining.
claims.notes: Online update reward assumptions and training setup are paper-specific.

claims.claim: AC-ODM develops actor-critic-based dynamic data mixing for language-model pretraining and evaluates it in the paper's reported setup.
claims.notes: Do not copy paper speedups to untested models or budgets.

claims.claim: The exercise's mixture p_i=(1-epsilon)*softmax(s_i/T)+epsilon/K is normalized and provides a floor of epsilon/K for each of K domains.
claims.locator: Softmax definition; convex mixture with uniform distribution
claims.notes: The expression is original teaching mathematics and NOT an implementation of DoReMi, RegMix-D, ODM or AC-ODM.

claims.claim: The demonstrated stable softmax is implemented with max-shifted exponentials to avoid overflow and returns a probability distribution.
claims.notes: Tested utility computes only weights from externally defined scores; no training or reward estimation occurs.

claims.claim: Comparing static, offline and online mixtures requires controlling token budget, tokenizer, model architecture, data snapshot and evaluation protocol.
claims.notes: Engineering experimental-design recommendation, not a universal ranking of algorithms.
